title: Check captions of videos
user_impact: Deaf or hard-of-hearing users cannot perceive spoken content.
technical_impact: A rendered <video> has a <track kind="captions"> or kind="subtitles", but none of its files loads from the page origin as a caption format (.vtt or .srt), or the page embeds a third-party player (YouTube, Vimeo and similar) whose captions the tool cannot see, so spoken content may have no text equivalent; an untested manual-check note, because caption accuracy and timing cannot be checked automatically either way. A video without such a track is reported as media/video-captions-missing instead.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (H95, G87, F8); HTML §4.8.11.11 track
checks.applicability:
Pages with a rendered native <video> that has a <track kind="captions"|"subtitles">
child, or with a known video-platform embed iframe (YouTube, Vimeo and similar).
A video without such a track is media/video-captions-missing (#1182); like that
rule, a muted video without controls and a video under aria-hidden="true" are
left out, so the two rules split the videos by track presence and none is
reported by both.
checks.expectation:
Pass (positive signal, no finding) only when every such video has a caption
track whose src resolves same-origin as a caption file (.vtt/.srt or a vtt
content type) and the page embeds no third-party player. Anything less — a
caption track without src, one that does not resolve or is cross-origin, more
caption tracks than the probe budget of 10 checks, or a third-party embed — is
one page-level UNTESTED note: captions may exist in ways the tool cannot see
(platform players), so never a violation. A page whose videos all lack a
caption track is not applicable here; a video in a hidden panel is not
presented in this state.
